**Teased but absent:** A **Copilot Super App** was widely anticipated. Nadella mentioned it in passing: *"Come summer, we will be bringing coding to all knowledge work within one Copilot Super App... Chat, Cowork, and Code all in Copilot."* The app itself did not ship at Build.

---

### 3. M365 Copilot — Announcements & Status

#### Wave 3 (already announced March 9, 2026 — shipping through Build timeframe)
- Wave 3 brought agentic capabilities embedded directly into **Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Copilot Chat**
- Introduced **Cowork** — long-running, multi-step work powered by Anthropic's Claude (notable: third-party model integration named explicitly)
- Frontier program access from late March 2026; broader rollout continuing

#### No Wave 4 announced at Build 2026 — Wave 3 completion was the focus

#### New M365 Copilot features at Build 2026

**Licensing:**
- **Microsoft 365 E7 (ME7)** went GA May 1, 2026 — bundles E5 + M365 Copilot + Entra Suite + Agent 365. $99/user/month.

**Redesigned UI:**
- New design turns the static prompt box into a **task-aware workspace** — described as more connected and adaptive. See: [Microsoft 365 Blog, May 28](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2026/05/28/introducing-a-new-design-for-microsoft-365-copilot/)

**Agent capabilities per app:**
- **Word/Excel/PowerPoint:** Copilot Agent Mode is GA — plan, execute, and refine multi-step work inside productivity apps end-to-end (create decks, build spreadsheets, draft documents from conversation)
- **Outlook:** Copilot Chat now reasons over entire inbox, calendar, meetings, and enterprise data; users can add emails into prompt context directly from threads
- **Teams:** Copilot Chat expanding to chats, channels, calling, and meetings
- **SharePoint:** Dynamic filtering — selecting a source (Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, Azure DevOps, Google Drive, Jira, Confluence) surfaces relevant filters in real time

**Copilot Memory:**
- User-level preferences now in **public preview** for Copilot Business and Enterprise — captures communication style, tool stack, git conventions, etc.
- New **admin controls** for governance
- **/chronicle feature:** Turns session history into standup summaries, personalized tips, and custom instructions

**Copilot Pages:**
- **Suggested edits** arriving in Copilot Pages
- **Copilot Notebooks** can now pull references from emails and meetings
- Dynamic MCP tool discovery for agents (find the right tools at runtime)

**MCP / Connectors:**
- Federated connectors built on MCP bring live data from **Canva, HubSpot, Linear, LSEG, Moody's, Notion**

---

### 4. Microsoft Scout — New Personal Work Agent

- Launched at Build; available via Frontier program in private preview
- Built on **OpenClaw** (an open-source project originally hacked together by an Austrian developer in late 2025; Microsoft is contributing enterprise policy controls back upstream)
- Classified as an **"Autopilot"** — always-on, proactive agent
- Connects to Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint; grounds in chats, email, calendar, contacts
- Capabilities: meeting prep, scheduling conflict resolution, calendar blocking, risk flagging (stalled decisions), deliverable tracking
- Security: each agent runs under its own governed **Entra identity**, with Purview data protection enforced in-the-moment
- Requires: Frontier enrollment + Intune policy + opt-in attestation + GitHub Copilot license
- Source: [Microsoft 365 Blog](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2026/06/02/introducing-microsoft-scout-your-always-on-personal-agent/)

---

### 5. Microsoft IQ — Context Layer (GA)

**GA as of June 2, 2026.** This is the unified intelligence middleware sitting between enterprise data and agents.

| Component | Status | What it does |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| **Work IQ** | GA (public APIs flipped at Build) | Semantic understanding of M365 signals — emails, meetings, documents, chats — within the M365 trust boundary |
| **Fabric IQ** | GA, expanding | Structured business data from Fabric; now a first-party MCP tool in Agent 365; extending into Cowork + Copilot Chat (Power BI reports, semantic models) |
| **Foundry IQ** | GA | Knowledge base unifying Work IQ, Fabric IQ, File Search, Azure SQL, and MCP behind one SLA-backed retrieval endpoint |
| **Web IQ** | New at Build | AI-native web grounding — discovery, ranking, extraction from web pages, news, images, video. MCP-native, model-agnostic. Claims ~2.5x speed advantage over next competitor |

Microsoft IQ is available across GitHub Copilot, Azure AI Foundry, and Copilot Studio.

---

### 6. Agent 365

- **GA: May 1, 2026** (before Build)
- **Agent 365 SDK went GA at Build** — free, framework-agnostic, with packages for: Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, Azure AI Foundry
- **Agent 365 for local agents** extends Entra, Defender, and Purview into a single control plane for observing, governing, and securing agents across the estate
- **Copilot Credits** named as the consumption meter for agent work

---

### 7. MAI Models — New In-House Model Family

Microsoft announced 7 new in-house MAI models at Build 2026, marking a strategic shift to vertical integration away from OpenAI for core Copilot workloads:

| Model | Details | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| **MAI-Thinking-1** | 35B parameter reasoning model, 256K context window, built without distillation. Microsoft claims blind raters prefer it to Sonnet 4.6; matches Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro. Enterprise-targeted. | Private preview on Foundry |
| **MAI-Code-1** | Coding model tuned for GitHub/VS Code. Replaces GPT-4 for core autocomplete in GitHub Copilot. | GA in Copilot and VS Code |
| **MAI-Code-1-Flash** | 5B parameter model, inference-efficient, built for code completion in GitHub Copilot. | GA |
| **MAI-Image-2.5** | Multimodal image model | Announced |
| **MAI-Voice-2** | Voice model | Announced |
| **MAI-Transcribe-1.5** | Transcription model | Announced |
| (7th model) | Not specifically named in sources | Announced |

**Regarding GPT-5/o3:** No GPT-5 or o3 model integrations were announced at Build. However, **GPT-5.5 had already been added to M365 Copilot in the May 2026 update** (pre-Build). The Build 2026 model story was squarely about the in-house MAI family.

**Project Polaris:** GitHub Copilot's internal project to replace GPT-4 with MAI-Code-1; multi-agent orchestration shipped in VS Code.

---

### 8. GitHub Copilot — Key Changes

- **MAI-Code-1 / MAI-Code-1-Flash** replace GPT-4 for core autocomplete
- **GitHub Copilot app** — native desktop app in technical preview for Windows 11, Windows 11 on Arm, Mac, and Linux (requires GitHub Copilot subscription)
- **GitHub Copilot SDK** went GA in: Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, Java
- **Microsoft IQ** now available across GitHub Copilot for enterprise grounding
- Multi-agent workflows in VS Code shipped

---

### 9. Windows / Copilot+ PC Updates

**Strategic pivot:** Microsoft de-emphasized Copilot+ PC branding at Build. The Copilot+ PC brand was conspicuously absent from the keynote. The new direction is a **universal local AI platform** that runs agents and models across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs on any Windows hardware.

**Recall — Recall API:**
- New **Recall API** lets applications query the local semantic index built by Windows Recall without exposing raw screenshots — a significant privacy improvement
- All processing on-device; semantic index encrypted with Windows Hello biometric keys
- No raw content uploaded to Microsoft servers; telemetry is opt-out aggregate metrics only

**Windows Copilot Runtime:**
- Originally bundled with Copilot+ PCs, now opening to all Windows 11 installations with compatible NPUs
- New APIs for: text summarization, image generation, contextual reasoning — fully on-device

**Windows Development Configurations:**
- **GA at Build** — single config file that takes a fresh machine to a ready-to-code setup in minutes

**RTX Spark Dev Box:**
- New developer hardware announced (NVIDIA RTX Spark Dev Box) — compact workstation for local AI development

---

### 10. Project Solara

A significant architectural announcement beyond M365/Copilot specifically:

- **Project Solara** is a chip-to-cloud platform designed for devices that run AI agents instead of traditional applications
- OS: **Microsoft Device Ecosystem Platform (MDEP)**, built on AOSP (Android Open Source Project) rather than Windows
- Targets always-connected, low-power form factors
- Two reference hardware concepts shown: a smart corporate badge (touchscreen, fingerprint, microphones, camera) and a stationary desk companion (like an Echo Show, with facial recognition auth)
- Reference designs for hardware partners, not consumer products
- Positioned as the post-smartphone, post-app computing paradigm

---

Main tracks: AI Agents & Agentic Apps, Cloud Platform & Data, Model Training, Windows, Developer Tools, Responsible AI, Local AI.

- Full agent lifecycle: experimentation → secure enterprise deployment (Foundry Agent Service + Agent Framework)
- Local AI connecting Foundry, Windows, and Nvidia hardware
- Production-ready agents: distributable, monetizable offerings

## Microsoft Build 2026: Copilot Studio & Agent Builder — Full Research Report

**Research basis:** Official Microsoft blog posts (May/April 2026 Copilot Studio updates), Microsoft Learn release plan documentation, Microsoft Build 2026 news page, Agent Framework devblog, and tech journalism. Build 2026 was held in San Francisco, June 2-5, 2026.

---

### 1. Copilot Studio New Capabilities at Build 2026

The headline May 2026 Copilot Studio update (shipped around/at Build) hit three major areas:

**Computer-Using Agents (CUA) — GA May 7, 2026**
- Agents can interact directly with websites and desktop applications via UI automation — no APIs required
- Now includes: secure enterprise credential management, model selection per scenario, resilience when UIs change (adaptable rather than brittle scripts)
- Can now be embedded in multi-step workflows (Preview) — so you can combine API-based actions, human approvals, and UI automation in a single flow

**Redesigned Workflows Experience — Early Release (Preview)**
- New unified visual canvas replacing the old linear flow designer
- Intent-driven modular model: connect reusable "skills" (pre-built AI actions) through a dependency graph
- Supports dynamic branching on real-time context (e.g., detect frustrated tone → route to human agent)
- AI-powered actions baked in: classification, content generation, decision support

## Microsoft Build 2026 — Enterprise AI Briefing

**Conference date:** ~27 May–30 May 2026, San Francisco. Satya Nadella's framing: the shift from *consuming a frontier model* to *fully participating at the frontier*. Six-layer agent stack — compute, models, context, tools, runtime, security — ran through every announcement.

---

### 1. Power Platform AI Updates

**Power Automate (Release Wave 1, April–September 2026)**

- AI agent authoring, optimization, and **self-healing desktop flows** (GA): agents automatically adapt when target UIs change rather than breaking silently.
- **Copilot Studio-powered actions in cloud flows** (GA): low-code invocation of Studio agents inside Automate.
- **Object-centric process mining** (GA): models complex, interconnected processes beyond linear flows.
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for process intelligence**: exposes process data as a tool endpoint for external agents.
- **Consolidated governance reporting** across desktop and cloud flows.

**Power Apps**
- **Fabric Apps** (Build announcement): coding agents build custom web apps from a semantic model spec in a few prompts. Targets financial planning, inventory management, pricing optimization patterns.
- Broader AI features roll out under Release Wave 1; Power Apps AI feature depth details are in the full Wave 1 plan at learn.microsoft.com.

**AI Builder**
- AI Builder credits are being **sunset** — Microsoft Learn has an explicit "End of AI Builder credits" migration page (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ai-builder/endofaibcredits). Functionality is migrating into Copilot Studio and Foundry. Worth tracking for existing AI Builder deployments.

**Copilot Studio (May 2026 — coincides with Build)**

- **Computer-Using Agents** (GA): agents drive websites and desktop apps via UI without brittle scripts. Ships with enterprise credential management (no embedded credentials) and adaptive interface recovery.
- Computer-using agents now embeddable in multi-step workflows combining API calls, approvals, business logic, and UI automation.
- **MCP support in declarative agents** (GA): direct integration of SaaS and LoB systems via MCP standard.
- **New Workflows experience** and **real-time voice** for agents: generally available in May update.

**Pricing note for Power Platform agents**: Copilot Credits consumption model at **$0.01 per credit**, prepaid packs at lower per-credit cost. **Activation is OFF by default** in Microsoft Admin Center — requires deliberate opt-in for enterprise rollouts.

**Sources:** [Power Platform Release Wave 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/release-plan/2026wave1/) · [Power Automate Wave 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/release-plan/2026wave1/power-automate/) · [Copilot Studio May 2026](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/new-and-improved-computer-using-agents-a-new-workflows-experience-and-real-time-voice-experiences/) · [AI Builder credits sunset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ai-builder/endofaibcredits)

---

### 2. Azure AI Foundry Announcements

Foundry is the renamed Azure AI Studio (renamed early 2025) — now the unified development-to-production surface.

**GA at Build 2026:**

- **Foundry IQ knowledge bases**: replaces custom RAG pipelines with a single SLA-backed retrieval endpoint unifying Work IQ, Fabric IQ, File Search, Azure SQL, and MCP sources. No custom plumbing required.
- **Foundry Toolkit for VS Code**: agent creation, debugging, deployment in one place.
- **Voice Live**: real-time voice pipeline (speech recognition, TTS, turn detection, interruption handling, avatars).
- **Fireworks AI on Foundry**: open-model inference through a single Azure endpoint with enterprise SLAs, SOC 2 readiness, PTU Data Zone support, and day-zero access to new open models. No separate Fireworks contract.
- **Tracing and Evaluations**: OpenTelemetry-based across any framework (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK, MAF). One pipeline; evals linked back to the trace that generated them.
- **Purview Data Risk Signals in Foundry Control Plane**: real-time data security posture during agent testing.
- **Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0**: see section 8.

**GA expected early July 2026:**

- **Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service**: managed runtime with per-session VM sandboxing, persistent filesystem across scale events, scale-to-zero pricing, framework-agnostic deployment (MAF, LangGraph, GitHub Copilot SDK, custom SDKs — no rewrites).

**Public Preview:**

- **Toolboxes in Foundry**: unified tool management — web search, file search, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A protocol behind one endpoint.
- **Memory in Foundry Agent Service**: procedural, user, and session memory types.
- **Routines**: agent scheduling and timer execution.
- **Hosted voice agents**: orchestration with Voice Live.
- **Tool search**: intelligent tool selection at runtime.
- **Work IQ / Fabric IQ**: enterprise data grounding APIs.
- **Fine-tuning developer tier**: experimental model customization.
- **Guided Guardrail Setup**: questionnaire-driven security recommendations.
- **Rubric Evaluator**: auto-generated quality scoring with context-aware criteria (task success, tone, safety, cost, latency).
- **User Simulation**: automated multi-turn test conversation generation.
- **Multi-turn Evaluation**: captures context carryover, reasoning consistency, safety regression across long conversations.
- **MAI-Thinking-1**: in private preview on Foundry.

- **Agent ROI**: translates agent costs into task completion rates, time saved, cost efficiency.

**Model catalogue**: now 11,000+ models. Includes OpenAI GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.5 Pro, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5, MAI family, Fireworks open models, specialised small/vision/multimodal/multilingual/time-series models — all under one Azure billing relationship.

**Model availability in Foundry:**

- **GPT-5.5** in Foundry: $5/M input · $0.50/M cached · $30/M output. MACC-eligible.
- **GPT-5.5 Pro** in Foundry: $30/M input · $3/M cached · $180/M output.

- **Unified Model API** (public preview): simplifies multi-model architectures behind a single endpoint — intended to make model swapping easier as MAI models come online.

When MAI benchmarks equal or exceed OpenAI for a task, Microsoft routing logic will prefer MAI (lower cost; no third-party dependency). This is already wired into Microsoft 365 Copilot and Dynamics 365.

### 4. Microsoft Fabric AI Features

**GPU-accelerated Fabric Data Warehouse** (new, GA timeline unspecified): first fully managed data warehouse with built-in GPU acceleration. Internal benchmarks vs three external vendors: up to 7x faster for reporting and application workloads.

**Fabric IQ**: cross-domain semantic models define business metrics, KPIs, and relationships once, then serve all agents and Copilots consistently. This is the "business context layer" — structured data equivalent to what Work IQ does for M365 content.

**OneLake enhancements:**
- **Multi-cloud shortcuts**: agents query AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage without data duplication.
- **Automated sensitivity labeling at ingestion** using Azure AI.
- **Cross-domain semantic models**: shareable definitions across the enterprise.

**Fabric Apps**: AI-first custom web apps with Fabric as backend. Coding agents build from spec + semantic model.

**Data Factory — Airflow MCP**: agent-driven authoring and diagnostics for Airflow DAGs, unifying AI authoring across low-code and pro-code orchestration.

**Power BI agentic era**: natural language queries against semantic models; agents can surface insights without manual report building.

**Rayfin** (new): backend-as-a-service on Microsoft Fabric with GitHub-based workflows — positions Fabric as an application backend, not just an analytics layer.

### 5. Safety and Responsible AI

Microsoft gave Responsible AI its **own dedicated track** at Build 2026 — a notable structural signal.

**Hosted Agents — built-in content safety guardrails** (GA with Hosted Agents in July 2026): every prompt and response evaluated in real time by **Foundry Content Safety** using **Microsoft.DefaultV2** controls (Jailbreak, Content Safety, Protected Materials). No middleware to write.

Now extending to multi-turn with the new **Multi-turn Evaluation** (preview) to catch safety regression across long conversations.

**ASSERT** (open source, GA): Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing — policy-driven evaluation framework for evaluating agent behavior against defined safety requirements.

**Agent Control Specification (ACS)** (open standard, GA): portable framework for defining and enforcing governance policies across agent environments.

**Microsoft Responsible AI Standard (International, 2026)**: updated framework released. Details at AI Safety Directory.

- **GPT 5.2 for custom field extraction** (GA): improved accuracy on mixed layouts and domain-specific language.
- Expanded format support GA: .eml, .msg, .doc, .xls, .ppt, .odt, .ods, .odp.
- **Agentic understanding mode** for complex documents (Preview, July 2026).

**MAI model family** — all seven models will be open-sourced under permissive licenses for research and commercial use. Timeline tied to their respective preview-to-GA milestones.

**Aion-1.0-Instruct** (developer preview, Hugging Face release July 2026): smaller, faster, more efficient than Phi-4-mini for local/on-device use. Runs on limited GPU/CPU. This is the successor direction for the Phi small-model line.

**ASSERT** (open source, GA): safety evaluation framework (see section 5).

**Agent Control Specification** (open standard, GA): governance policy framework.

**Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (.NET and Python, GA April 2026): fully open source on GitHub.

**CodeAct with Hyperlight** (alpha): open-source micro-VM execution environment — 52.4% latency reduction, 63.9% token reduction by collapsing tool calls into single Python programs in isolated micro-VMs.

### 7. MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

MCP is now a **first-class architectural primitive** across the Microsoft stack, not just a compatibility layer:

- **Copilot Studio declarative agents with MCP** (GA): connects M365 Copilot to SaaS and LoB systems via MCP servers.
- **Foundry Toolboxes** (preview): MCP exposed alongside OpenAPI, A2A, web search, and file search behind one endpoint.
- **Foundry IQ** (GA): MCP is one of the unified retrieval sources behind the knowledge endpoint.
- **Power Automate Process Intelligence MCP server**: exposes process mining data to external agents.
- **Microsoft 365 Teams SDK**: MCP + A2A built-in.
- **Work IQ APIs**: support A2A, MCP, REST.
- **Windows 11**: dedicated MCP on Windows documentation (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/mcp/overview) — MCP as a Windows platform capability.
- **Agent 365 registry**: discovers and governs MCP servers via Defender/Entra/Intune.
- **Visual Studio 2022**: receiving VS 2026 MCP functionality backported.
- **Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agents with MCP**: MCP specification RC coming 2026-07-28.

**Sources:** [M365 Dev Blog MCP](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/build-declarative-agents-for-microsoft-365-copilot-with-mcp/) · [MCP on Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/mcp/overview) · [MCP Spec RC](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)

### 8. AI Orchestration Frameworks / SDK Updates

**Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (GA April 2, 2026 — highlighted at Build):

- The **convergence of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel** into a single production platform. AutoGen receives security/bug fixes only; Semantic Kernel active but MAF is the recommended path for new agent work.
- Unified concepts and APIs across **.NET and Python**.
- **Agent Harness** (GA): context compaction, FileMemoryProvider, FileAccessProvider, TodoProvider, AgentModeProvider, AgentSkillsProvider, BackgroundAgentsProvider, web search and shell execution.
- **Multi-agent handoff orchestration** (1.0): developer-defined topology + agent-driven routing. Framework-agnostic.
- **GitHub Copilot SDK integration** (1.0): MAF agents backed by Copilot with shell execution, file ops, URL fetching, MCP server integration.
- **CodeAct with Hyperlight** (alpha): micro-VM execution, 52.4% latency reduction, 63.9% token reduction.
- **Procedural memory** and **Voice Live** integration in preview.

**Foundry Hosted Agents** (GA July 2026): MAF is the native runtime, but any framework deploys without rewrites.

**Semantic Kernel**: still active with recent releases. Not deprecated, but MAF is the forward investment.

**AutoGen**: maintenance mode — bug fixes and critical security patches only.

**Sources:** [Agent Framework Build 2026 Announce](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/microsoft-agent-framework-at-build-2026-announce/) · [MAF convergence article](https://cloudsummit.eu/blog/microsoft-agent-framework-production-ready-convergence-autogen-semantic-kernel)

### 9. Enterprise Security and Compliance for AI

This was a major theme with its own dedicated Build track.

**Agent 365 SDK** (GA): observability, access controls, compliance enforcement baked into development workflows. Integrates Defender, Entra, Intune, and Purview controls at the agent layer.

**Microsoft Execution Container (MXC) SDK** (Early Preview): OS-level process and session isolation for agent execution — the sandboxing primitive underneath several agent platforms.

**Windows 365 for Agents** (GA): fully isolated, policy-governed Cloud PC environments specifically for agent execution. Consumption-based pricing.

**Agent 365 Agent Registry** (Preview): discovers 20+ local agent types. Intune policies can block specific agent execution methods. Discovery via Defender, Entra, and Intune.

**Microsoft Purview for Agents** (Preview): data exfiltration prevention, Data Security Posture Management, runtime DLP for prompts and responses, agentic risk detection.

**Purview Data Risk Signals in Foundry Control Plane** (GA): real-time data security posture visible during agent testing — before production.

**Runtime DLP for Agent Prompts** (Preview): detects, blocks, and audits sensitive data before it's processed by an agent.

**MDASH — Multi-Model Agentic Scanning Harness** (Expanded Preview): orchestrates 100+ specialized AI agents across an ensemble of models to discover, validate, and prove exploitability across codebases. Scored 96.55% on CyberGym benchmark. Integrates with Microsoft Defender.

**Microsoft Defender + GitHub Code Security** (GA): runtime-enriched vulnerability findings with real production signals (internet exposure, data sensitivity), AI-assisted fixes via GitHub Copilot Autofix.

**Defender AI Model Scanning** (Preview): inspects model artifacts across registries, workspaces, and CI/CD pipelines before deployment.

**Entra ID Conditional Access for agents**: treats every agent action as a potential identity boundary crossing. New controls specifically for agentic workloads.

### 10. Competitive Messaging vs OpenAI / Google / Anthropic

Microsoft's positioning at Build 2026 was the most explicitly competitive in years:

**On OpenAI**: The relationship is continuing but Microsoft is deliberately reducing dependency. "Project Polaris" is the internal initiative to route MAI models in place of OpenAI models where performance is equivalent or better, with projected **10x cost efficiency** vs GPT-5.5 after MAI tuning for specific workloads (McKinsey case cited by Mustafa Suleyman). Satya Nadella said: *"We believe the time has come for every company to move from consuming a frontier model to fully participating at the frontier."*

**MAI-Thinking-1 vs Anthropic**: In blind evaluations run by Surge (independent rating partner), MAI-Thinking-1 was **preferred over Claude Sonnet 4.6** and matches **Claude Opus 4.6 on coding**. This was stated publicly by Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman.

**MAI-Code vs OpenAI/Meta**: MAI-Code (15B parameter) outperforms **OpenAI Codex and Meta Code Llama** on HumanEval and MBPP benchmarks. Coding tools are explicitly called out as the battleground where Microsoft is challenging Anthropic and OpenAI.

**Microsoft AI Chief's direct statement**: Mustafa Suleyman said Microsoft is *"less concerned"* about Google, Meta, and OpenAI as the Anthropic battle heats up — signalling Anthropic as the primary benchmark competitor.

**Foundry model catalogue breadth**: with 11,000+ models including Anthropic and OpenAI models alongside MAI and open-source alternatives, Microsoft is positioning Foundry as the **model-neutral enterprise AI platform** — developers choose the model, Azure provides the control plane, observability, security, and billing. This is a deliberate counter to single-vendor lock-in narratives from OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise) and Google (Vertex AI).

**Google competition**: Microsoft and Google are explicitly competing on coding model performance. Surface RTX Spark Dev Box with 120B parameter local capability is a direct counter to Google's on-device AI investments.

**Sources:** [CNBC Microsoft MAI vs OpenAI](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/microsoft-unveils-new-ai-models-lessen-reliance-on-openai-lower-costs.html) · [Storyboard18 competitive analysis](https://www.storyboard18.com/digital/5-big-ai-announcements-from-microsoft-build-2026-as-company-sharpens-rivalry-with-openai-anthropic-100079.htm) · [Benzinga Suleyman quote](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/06/52966889/microsofts-ai-chief-says-company-is-less-concerned-about-google-meta-and-openai-as-anthropic-battle-heats-up-weve-closed-an-enormous-gap) · [GeekWire self-sufficiency](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsoft-unveils-seven-homegrown-ai-models-in-bid-for-long-term-self-sufficiency/)

---

### Key Architectural Signals for an Enterprise Architect

A few patterns worth tracking separately from the feature list:

1. **AI Builder credits are being sunset** — if your estate uses AI Builder, migration planning is needed now.

2. **Foundry is the new Azure AI control plane** — Azure AI Studio branding is gone. If you have Azure AI Studio deployments or training, the Foundry migration path is the strategic direction.

3. **AutoGen → Microsoft Agent Framework** — AutoGen is in maintenance. Any active AutoGen development should assess the MAF migration path.

4. **MCP is infrastructure, not a feature** — Microsoft is wiring MCP across Copilot Studio, Foundry, Teams, Windows, and Visual Studio simultaneously. It's becoming the plumbing standard for tool/context integration.

5. **"Pay-as-you-go OFF by default"** for Copilot Credits — this is a governance lever. Enterprise rollouts need deliberate activation planning.

6. **Purview + Entra + Defender now cover agents natively** — the security perimeter is being extended to agent identities and actions. Worth aligning with your security team early on any Copilot Studio or MAF agent deployments.

7. **MAI routing replacing OpenAI calls** — this will happen automatically in M365 Copilot and Dynamics 365 where benchmarks favour MAI. Not a choice; it's platform behavior.

## Microsoft Build 2026 — Enterprise AI Briefing

**Conference date:** ~27 May–30 May 2026, San Francisco. Satya Nadella's framing: the shift from *consuming a frontier model* to *fully participating at the frontier*. Six-layer agent stack — compute, models, context, tools, runtime, security — ran through every announcement.

---

### 1. Power Platform AI Updates

**Power Automate (Release Wave 1, April–September 2026)**

- AI agent authoring, optimization, and **self-healing desktop flows** (GA): agents automatically adapt when target UIs change rather than breaking silently.
- **Copilot Studio-powered actions in cloud flows** (GA): low-code invocation of Studio agents inside Automate.
- **Object-centric process mining** (GA): models complex, interconnected processes beyond linear flows.
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for process intelligence**: exposes process data as a tool endpoint for external agents.
- **Consolidated governance reporting** across desktop and cloud flows.

**Power Apps**
- **Fabric Apps** (Build announcement): coding agents build custom web apps from a semantic model spec in a few prompts. Targets financial planning, inventory management, pricing optimization patterns.
- Broader AI features roll out under Release Wave 1; Power Apps AI feature depth details are in the full Wave 1 plan at learn.microsoft.com.

**AI Builder**
- AI Builder credits are being **sunset** — Microsoft Learn has an explicit "End of AI Builder credits" migration page (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ai-builder/endofaibcredits). Functionality is migrating into Copilot Studio and Foundry. Worth tracking for existing AI Builder deployments.

**Copilot Studio (May 2026 — coincides with Build)**

- **Computer-Using Agents** (GA): agents drive websites and desktop apps via UI without brittle scripts. Ships with enterprise credential management (no embedded credentials) and adaptive interface recovery.
- Computer-using agents now embeddable in multi-step workflows combining API calls, approvals, business logic, and UI automation.
- **MCP support in declarative agents** (GA): direct integration of SaaS and LoB systems via MCP standard.
- **New Workflows experience** and **real-time voice** for agents: generally available in May update.

**Pricing note for Power Platform agents**: Copilot Credits consumption model at **$0.01 per credit**, prepaid packs at lower per-credit cost. **Activation is OFF by default** in Microsoft Admin Center — requires deliberate opt-in for enterprise rollouts.

**Sources:** [Power Platform Release Wave 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/release-plan/2026wave1/) · [Power Automate Wave 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/release-plan/2026wave1/power-automate/) · [Copilot Studio May 2026](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/new-and-improved-computer-using-agents-a-new-workflows-experience-and-real-time-voice-experiences/) · [AI Builder credits sunset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ai-builder/endofaibcredits)

---

### 2. Azure AI Foundry Announcements

Foundry is the renamed Azure AI Studio (renamed early 2025) — now the unified development-to-production surface.

**GA at Build 2026:**

- **Foundry IQ knowledge bases**: replaces custom RAG pipelines with a single SLA-backed retrieval endpoint unifying Work IQ, Fabric IQ, File Search, Azure SQL, and MCP sources. No custom plumbing required.
- **Foundry Toolkit for VS Code**: agent creation, debugging, deployment in one place.
- **Voice Live**: real-time voice pipeline (speech recognition, TTS, turn detection, interruption handling, avatars).
- **Fireworks AI on Foundry**: open-model inference through a single Azure endpoint with enterprise SLAs, SOC 2 readiness, PTU Data Zone support, and day-zero access to new open models. No separate Fireworks contract.
- **Tracing and Evaluations**: OpenTelemetry-based across any framework (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK, MAF). One pipeline; evals linked back to the trace that generated them.
- **Purview Data Risk Signals in Foundry Control Plane**: real-time data security posture during agent testing.
- **Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0**: see section 8.

**GA expected early July 2026:**

- **Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service**: managed runtime with per-session VM sandboxing, persistent filesystem across scale events, scale-to-zero pricing, framework-agnostic deployment (MAF, LangGraph, GitHub Copilot SDK, custom SDKs — no rewrites).

**Public Preview:**

- **Toolboxes in Foundry**: unified tool management — web search, file search, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A protocol behind one endpoint.
- **Memory in Foundry Agent Service**: procedural, user, and session memory types.
- **Routines**: agent scheduling and timer execution.
- **Hosted voice agents**: orchestration with Voice Live.
- **Tool search**: intelligent tool selection at runtime.
- **Work IQ / Fabric IQ**: enterprise data grounding APIs.
- **Fine-tuning developer tier**: experimental model customization.
- **Guided Guardrail Setup**: questionnaire-driven security recommendations.
- **Rubric Evaluator**: auto-generated quality scoring with context-aware criteria (task success, tone, safety, cost, latency).
- **User Simulation**: automated multi-turn test conversation generation.
- **Multi-turn Evaluation**: captures context carryover, reasoning consistency, safety regression across long conversations.
- **MAI-Thinking-1**: in private preview on Foundry.

**Private Preview:**

- **Agent Optimizer**: turns production observability signals into ranked improvement candidates (prompt, tools, skills, context).
- **Agent ROI**: translates agent costs into task completion rates, time saved, cost efficiency.

**Model catalogue**: now 11,000+ models. Includes OpenAI GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.5 Pro, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5, MAI family, Fireworks open models, specialised small/vision/multimodal/multilingual/time-series models — all under one Azure billing relationship.

**Sources:** [What's New in Microsoft Foundry Build 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/whats-new-in-microsoft-foundry-build-2026/) · [Foundry Agent Service Build 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/agent-service-build2026/) · [Observability to ROI](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/build-2026-from-observability-to-roi-for-ai-agents-on-any-framework/)

---

### 3. Azure OpenAI Service Updates

The clearest signal at Build 2026 is that "Azure OpenAI Service" as a distinct brand is being absorbed into **Microsoft Foundry** as the deployment surface. GPT models are still central — Satya Nadella and Kevin Scott both reiterated the partnership — but the architecture is shifting.

**Model availability in Foundry:**

- **GPT-5.5** in Foundry: $5/M input · $0.50/M cached · $30/M output. MACC-eligible.
- **GPT-5.5 Pro** in Foundry: $30/M input · $3/M cached · $180/M output.
- New fine-tuning and inference features for GPT-5 coming in Azure (timeline not locked).
- **Unified Model API** (public preview): simplifies multi-model architectures behind a single endpoint — intended to make model swapping easier as MAI models come online.

**Strategic context — "Project Polaris"**: Microsoft is actively building MAI models as routing alternatives to OpenAI, with the stated goal of "long-term self-sufficiency." When MAI benchmarks equal or exceed OpenAI for a task, Microsoft routing logic will prefer MAI (lower cost; no third-party dependency). This is already wired into Microsoft 365 Copilot and Dynamics 365.

**Sources:** [CNBC — Microsoft unveils MAI models](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/microsoft-unveils-new-ai-models-lessen-reliance-on-openai-lower-costs.html) · [Windows News — Project Polaris](https://windowsnews.ai/article/microsoft-build-2026-how-redmond-plans-to-wean-azure-off-openai-dependence.421844) · [Foundry May docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/whats-new-foundry)

---

### 4. Microsoft Fabric AI Features

**GPU-accelerated Fabric Data Warehouse** (new, GA timeline unspecified): first fully managed data warehouse with built-in GPU acceleration. Internal benchmarks vs three external vendors: up to 7x faster for reporting and application workloads.

**Fabric IQ**: cross-domain semantic models define business metrics, KPIs, and relationships once, then serve all agents and Copilots consistently. This is the "business context layer" — structured data equivalent to what Work IQ does for M365 content.

**OneLake enhancements:**
- **Multi-cloud shortcuts**: agents query AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage without data duplication.
- **Automated sensitivity labeling at ingestion** using Azure AI.
- **Cross-domain semantic models**: shareable definitions across the enterprise.

**Fabric Apps**: AI-first custom web apps with Fabric as backend. Coding agents build from spec + semantic model.

**Data Factory — Airflow MCP**: agent-driven authoring and diagnostics for Airflow DAGs, unifying AI authoring across low-code and pro-code orchestration.

**Power BI agentic era**: natural language queries against semantic models; agents can surface insights without manual report building.

**Rayfin** (new): backend-as-a-service on Microsoft Fabric with GitHub-based workflows — positions Fabric as an application backend, not just an analytics layer.

**Sources:** [Fabric Azure Blog](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/microsoft-build-2026-building-agentic-apps-with-microsoft-fabric-and-microsoft-databases/) · [Fabric Community](https://community.fabric.microsoft.com/t5/Fabric-Updates-Blog/Build-2026-From-data-to-intelligence-Faster-with-Fabric-Data/ba-p/5191636) · [Power BI Build 2026](https://community.fabric.microsoft.com/t5/Power-BI-Updates-Blog/Power-BI-at-Microsoft-Build-2026-The-Agentic-Era-of-analytics/ba-p/5191671)

---

### 5. Safety and Responsible AI

Microsoft gave Responsible AI its **own dedicated track** at Build 2026 — a notable structural signal.

**Hosted Agents — built-in content safety guardrails** (GA with Hosted Agents in July 2026): every prompt and response evaluated in real time by **Foundry Content Safety** using **Microsoft.DefaultV2** controls (Jailbreak, Content Safety, Protected Materials). No middleware to write.

**Safety Evaluations framework** (in Foundry, existing): hateful/unfair content, sexual content, violent content, self-harm, direct and indirect jailbreak, protected material. Now extending to multi-turn with the new **Multi-turn Evaluation** (preview) to catch safety regression across long conversations.

**ASSERT** (open source, GA): Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing — policy-driven evaluation framework for evaluating agent behavior against defined safety requirements.

**Agent Control Specification (ACS)** (open standard, GA): portable framework for defining and enforcing governance policies across agent environments.

**Microsoft Responsible AI Standard (International, 2026)**: updated framework released. Details at AI Safety Directory.

**Azure Content Understanding at Build 2026:**
- **GPT 5.2 for custom field extraction** (GA): improved accuracy on mixed layouts and domain-specific language.
- Expanded format support GA: .eml, .msg, .doc, .xls, .ppt, .odt, .ods, .odp.
- **Agentic understanding mode** for complex documents (Preview, July 2026).

**Sources:** [Microsoft Security Blog Build 2026](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/microsoft-build-2026-securing-code-agents-and-models-across-the-development-lifecycle/) · [Foundry Safety Evaluations Transparency Note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/safety-evaluations-transparency-note) · [Content Understanding Build 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/whats-new-in-azure-content-understanding-at-build-2026/) · [AI Safety Directory](https://aisecurityandsafety.org/en/frameworks/microsoft-responsible-ai-standard/)

---

### 6. Open Source Releases

**MAI model family** — all seven models will be open-sourced under permissive licenses for research and commercial use. Timeline tied to their respective preview-to-GA milestones.

**Aion-1.0-Instruct** (developer preview, Hugging Face release July 2026): smaller, faster, more efficient than Phi-4-mini for local/on-device use. Runs on limited GPU/CPU. This is the successor direction for the Phi small-model line.

**Phi-4 family**: ongoing — the Phi product page confirms continued development, but Build 2026 was dominated by the MAI brand rather than new Phi releases specifically.

**ASSERT** (open source, GA): safety evaluation framework (see section 5).

**Agent Control Specification** (open standard, GA): governance policy framework.

**Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (.NET and Python, GA April 2026): fully open source on GitHub.

**CodeAct with Hyperlight** (alpha): open-source micro-VM execution environment — 52.4% latency reduction, 63.9% token reduction by collapsing tool calls into single Python programs in isolated micro-VMs.

**Sources:** [MAI Models CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/microsoft-unveils-new-ai-models-lessen-reliance-on-openai-lower-costs.html) · [MAI Windows News](https://windowsnews.ai/article/microsoft-mai-models-at-build-2026-in-house-reasoning-image-voice-and-coding.423377) · [Agent Framework Build 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/microsoft-agent-framework-at-build-2026-announce/)

---

### 7. MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

MCP is now a **first-class architectural primitive** across the Microsoft stack, not just a compatibility layer:

- **Copilot Studio declarative agents with MCP** (GA): connects M365 Copilot to SaaS and LoB systems via MCP servers.
- **Foundry Toolboxes** (preview): MCP exposed alongside OpenAPI, A2A, web search, and file search behind one endpoint.
- **Foundry IQ** (GA): MCP is one of the unified retrieval sources behind the knowledge endpoint.
- **Power Automate Process Intelligence MCP server**: exposes process mining data to external agents.
- **Microsoft 365 Teams SDK**: MCP + A2A built-in.
- **Work IQ APIs**: support A2A, MCP, REST.
- **Windows 11**: dedicated MCP on Windows documentation (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/mcp/overview) — MCP as a Windows platform capability.
- **Agent 365 registry**: discovers and governs MCP servers via Defender/Entra/Intune.
- **Visual Studio 2022**: receiving VS 2026 MCP functionality backported.
- **Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agents with MCP**: MCP specification RC coming 2026-07-28.

**Sources:** [M365 Dev Blog MCP](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/microsoft365dev/build-declarative-agents-for-microsoft-365-copilot-with-mcp/) · [MCP on Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ai/mcp/overview) · [MCP Spec RC](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/)

---

### 8. AI Orchestration Frameworks / SDK Updates

**Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0** (GA April 2, 2026 — highlighted at Build):

- The **convergence of AutoGen and Semantic Kernel** into a single production platform. AutoGen receives security/bug fixes only; Semantic Kernel active but MAF is the recommended path for new agent work.
- Unified concepts and APIs across **.NET and Python**.
- **Agent Harness** (GA): context compaction, FileMemoryProvider, FileAccessProvider, TodoProvider, AgentModeProvider, AgentSkillsProvider, BackgroundAgentsProvider, web search and shell execution.
- **Multi-agent handoff orchestration** (1.0): developer-defined topology + agent-driven routing. Framework-agnostic.
- **GitHub Copilot SDK integration** (1.0): MAF agents backed by Copilot with shell execution, file ops, URL fetching, MCP server integration.
- **CodeAct with Hyperlight** (alpha): micro-VM execution, 52.4% latency reduction, 63.9% token reduction.
- **Procedural memory** and **Voice Live** integration in preview.

**Foundry Hosted Agents** (GA July 2026): MAF is the native runtime, but any framework deploys without rewrites.

**Semantic Kernel**: still active with recent releases. Not deprecated, but MAF is the forward investment.

**AutoGen**: maintenance mode — bug fixes and critical security patches only.

**Sources:** [Agent Framework Build 2026 Announce](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/microsoft-agent-framework-at-build-2026-announce/) · [MAF convergence article](https://cloudsummit.eu/blog/microsoft-agent-framework-production-ready-convergence-autogen-semantic-kernel)

---

### 9. Enterprise Security and Compliance for AI

This was a major theme with its own dedicated Build track.

**Agent 365 SDK** (GA): observability, access controls, compliance enforcement baked into development workflows. Integrates Defender, Entra, Intune, and Purview controls at the agent layer.

**Microsoft Execution Container (MXC) SDK** (Early Preview): OS-level process and session isolation for agent execution — the sandboxing primitive underneath several agent platforms.

**Windows 365 for Agents** (GA): fully isolated, policy-governed Cloud PC environments specifically for agent execution. Consumption-based pricing.

**Agent 365 Agent Registry** (Preview): discovers 20+ local agent types. Intune policies can block specific agent execution methods. Discovery via Defender, Entra, and Intune.

**Microsoft Purview for Agents** (Preview): data exfiltration prevention, Data Security Posture Management, runtime DLP for prompts and responses, agentic risk detection.

**Purview Data Risk Signals in Foundry Control Plane** (GA): real-time data security posture visible during agent testing — before production.

**Runtime DLP for Agent Prompts** (Preview): detects, blocks, and audits sensitive data before it's processed by an agent.

**MDASH — Multi-Model Agentic Scanning Harness** (Expanded Preview): orchestrates 100+ specialized AI agents across an ensemble of models to discover, validate, and prove exploitability across codebases. Scored 96.55% on CyberGym benchmark. Integrates with Microsoft Defender.

**Microsoft Defender + GitHub Code Security** (GA): runtime-enriched vulnerability findings with real production signals (internet exposure, data sensitivity), AI-assisted fixes via GitHub Copilot Autofix.

**Defender AI Model Scanning** (Preview): inspects model artifacts across registries, workspaces, and CI/CD pipelines before deployment.

**Entra ID Conditional Access for agents**: treats every agent action as a potential identity boundary crossing. New controls specifically for agentic workloads.

**Sources:** [Microsoft Security Blog Build 2026](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/microsoft-build-2026-securing-code-agents-and-models-across-the-development-lifecycle/) · [theCUBE Research governance](https://thecuberesearch.com/what-microsoft-build-2026-means-for-ai-agent-security-and-governance/) · [CSO Online agent security](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4180467/microsoft-wants-to-put-ai-agents-on-a-short-leash.html)

---

### 10. Competitive Messaging vs OpenAI / Google / Anthropic

Microsoft's positioning at Build 2026 was the most explicitly competitive in years:

**On OpenAI**: The relationship is continuing but Microsoft is deliberately reducing dependency. "Project Polaris" is the internal initiative to route MAI models in place of OpenAI models where performance is equivalent or better, with projected **10x cost efficiency** vs GPT-5.5 after MAI tuning for specific workloads (McKinsey case cited by Mustafa Suleyman). Satya Nadella said: *"We believe the time has come for every company to move from consuming a frontier model to fully participating at the frontier."*

**MAI-Thinking-1 vs Anthropic**: In blind evaluations run by Surge (independent rating partner), MAI-Thinking-1 was **preferred over Claude Sonnet 4.6** and matches **Claude Opus 4.6 on coding**. This was stated publicly by Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman.

**MAI-Code vs OpenAI/Meta**: MAI-Code (15B parameter) outperforms **OpenAI Codex and Meta Code Llama** on HumanEval and MBPP benchmarks. Coding tools are explicitly called out as the battleground where Microsoft is challenging Anthropic and OpenAI.

**Microsoft AI Chief's direct statement**: Mustafa Suleyman said Microsoft is *"less concerned"* about Google, Meta, and OpenAI as the Anthropic battle heats up — signalling Anthropic as the primary benchmark competitor.

**Foundry model catalogue breadth**: with 11,000+ models including Anthropic and OpenAI models alongside MAI and open-source alternatives, Microsoft is positioning Foundry as the **model-neutral enterprise AI platform** — developers choose the model, Azure provides the control plane, observability, security, and billing. This is a deliberate counter to single-vendor lock-in narratives from OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise) and Google (Vertex AI).

**Google competition**: Microsoft and Google are explicitly competing on coding model performance. Surface RTX Spark Dev Box with 120B parameter local capability is a direct counter to Google's on-device AI investments.

**Sources:** [CNBC Microsoft MAI vs OpenAI](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/microsoft-unveils-new-ai-models-lessen-reliance-on-openai-lower-costs.html) · [Storyboard18 competitive analysis](https://www.storyboard18.com/digital/5-big-ai-announcements-from-microsoft-build-2026-as-company-sharpens-rivalry-with-openai-anthropic-100079.htm) · [Benzinga Suleyman quote](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/06/52966889/microsofts-ai-chief-says-company-is-less-concerned-about-google-meta-and-openai-as-anthropic-battle-heats-up-weve-closed-an-enormous-gap) · [GeekWire self-sufficiency](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsoft-unveils-seven-homegrown-ai-models-in-bid-for-long-term-self-sufficiency/)

---

### Key Architectural Signals for an Enterprise Architect

A few patterns worth tracking separately from the feature list:

1. **AI Builder credits are being sunset** — if your estate uses AI Builder, migration planning is needed now.

2. **Foundry is the new Azure AI control plane** — Azure AI Studio branding is gone. If you have Azure AI Studio deployments or training, the Foundry migration path is the strategic direction.

3. **AutoGen → Microsoft Agent Framework** — AutoGen is in maintenance. Any active AutoGen development should assess the MAF migration path.

4. **MCP is infrastructure, not a feature** — Microsoft is wiring MCP across Copilot Studio, Foundry, Teams, Windows, and Visual Studio simultaneously. It's becoming the plumbing standard for tool/context integration.

5. **"Pay-as-you-go OFF by default"** for Copilot Credits — this is a governance lever. Enterprise rollouts need deliberate activation planning.

6. **Purview + Entra + Defender now cover agents natively** — the security perimeter is being extended to agent identities and actions. Worth aligning with your security team early on any Copilot Studio or MAF agent deployments.

7. **MAI routing replacing OpenAI calls** — this will happen automatically in M365 Copilot and Dynamics 365 where benchmarks favour MAI. Not a choice; it's platform behavior.

Base directory for this skill: /home/jellypai/.claude/skills/ApertureOscillation

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/ApertureOscillation/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


# ApertureOscillation

**3-pass scope oscillation that varies the zoom level of how a question is framed — narrow tactical, wide strategic, then synthesis — to surface design tensions invisible at any single scope.**

Grounded in the observation that LLMs (and humans) produce fundamentally different outputs depending on the scope of the framing context. A component designed in isolation has its own logic. The same component designed within a stated system vision inherits different constraints. The delta between these two framings is where the real insight lives.

## Core Concept

Instead of rotating analytical lenses (IterativeDepth) or generating divergent ideas (BeCreative), ApertureOscillation holds the question constant but shifts the **scope envelope** around it across 3 structured passes:

1. **Narrow Aperture (Tactical-first):** The specific thing is primary. Big-picture context is background. This captures what the component naturally wants to be — its own internal logic and shape.

2. **Wide Aperture (Strategic-first):** The vision/system goal is primary. The specific thing is derived from it. This captures what the system needs the component to be — coherence, alignment, constraints you'd miss thinking locally.

3. **Oscillation (Synthesis):** Feed both outputs. Ask where the tactical and strategic views diverge. The tensions, gaps, and surprises between the two framings are the output — the things neither pass alone would surface.

## How It Differs from IterativeDepth

| Dimension | IterativeDepth | ApertureOscillation |
|-----------|---------------|---------------------|
| **What varies** | Analytical lens (failure, stakeholder, temporal...) | Scope/zoom level (narrow, wide, synthesized) |
| **Pass count** | 2-8 | 3 (fixed) |
| **Input** | Single problem statement | Two inputs: tactical target + strategic context |
| **Output** | Richer requirements from multiple angles | Design tensions between local and system-level views |
| **Best for** | Requirement discovery, blind spot elimination | Architecture decisions, feature design, system coherence |
| **When to combine** | Use IterativeDepth first (understand the problem), then ApertureOscillation (understand where the solution fits) |

## Use / Win

**When to use:** Any time you're building something specific within a larger system and need to ensure the local design serves the global vision — without losing the component's own logic.

Concrete triggers:
- **Architecture decisions** — "Should this be a service, a library, or inline?" depends entirely on whether you're zoomed into the component or zoomed out to the system.
- **Feature design** — The feature a user asks for vs. the feature the product needs are often subtly different. Oscillation surfaces the gap.
- **System coherence checks** — When adding to existing infrastructure, the new piece must serve both its own purpose and the system's. Single-scope framing misses one or the other.
- **Design reviews** — Before committing to an approach, oscillate scope to check that the tactical plan and the strategic vision agree.
- **Scope negotiation** — When the user says "build X" and X could be simple or complex depending on context, oscillation reveals which scope is appropriate.

**What you win:**
- **Design tensions surfaced before they become mid-build surprises.** The most expensive rework comes from a component that works perfectly on its own but doesn't serve the system.
- **Scope clarity.** Seeing the same question at narrow and wide aperture often reveals that the obvious scope is wrong.
- **Coherence confidence.** When tactical and strategic views align, you can build with conviction. When they diverge, you know exactly where to make tradeoffs.

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger | Workflow |
|---------|----------|
| "aperture oscillation", "oscillate scope", "zoom in/out", "tactical vs strategic" | `Workflows/Oscillate.md` |
| Algorithm OBSERVE/THINK selects ApertureOscillation capability | `Workflows/Oscillate.md` |

## Quick Reference

- **3 passes** — always 3 (narrow, wide, synthesis)
- **2 inputs** — tactical target (what you're building) + strategic context (why, the bigger picture)
- **Output** — design tensions, scope recommendations, coherence assessment
- **Integration point** — OBSERVE (before ISC) or THINK (before approach commitment)

## Gotchas

- **Requires two distinct inputs.** If the tactical target and strategic context are the same thing, ApertureOscillation adds no value — use IterativeDepth instead.
- **3 passes is the right number.** Unlike IterativeDepth (2-8), the narrow/wide/synthesis structure is complete at 3. Adding passes would just be lens rotation, which is IterativeDepth's job.
- **The synthesis pass is where the value lives.** Passes 1 and 2 are setup. If the synthesis finds no divergence, that's a valid (and valuable) finding — it means the tactical and strategic views are already aligned.
- **This is a BPE-fragile skill.** Monitor whether smarter models naturally oscillate scope without being prompted. Quarterly test recommended.

## Examples

**Example 1: Feature design within a system**
```
Tactical target: "Build a caching layer for session data"
Strategic context: "PAI is a Life OS that needs responsive, session-spanning AI assistance"

Pass 1 (Narrow): Redis with TTL, standard session cache patterns
Pass 2 (Wide): Cache must survive session boundaries, integrate with memory system, serve the Life OS vision
Pass 3 (Synthesis): Tension — standard session cache expires data that the Life OS needs to persist. Resolution: hybrid cache with session-scoped fast layer + memory-backed persistent layer.
```

**Example 2: Architecture decision**
```
Tactical target: "Add webhook support to the Feed system"
Strategic context: "Feed is one pipeline in Arbol, which processes content for Surface"

Pass 1 (Narrow): Standard webhook receiver, queue, retry logic
Pass 2 (Wide): Webhooks must flow through Arbol's action/function pattern, integrate with existing queue infrastructure
Pass 3 (Synthesis): Tension — standalone webhook service vs. Arbol action. Resolution: implement as Arbol action, not standalone service, because the strategic context demands pipeline coherence over component independence.
```

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"ApertureOscillation","workflow":"Oscillate","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

Replace `8_WORD_SUMMARY` with a brief input description, and `SECONDS` with approximate wall-clock time. Log `status: "error"` if the workflow failed.

# Microsoft Build 2026 — Copilot Ecosystem Briefing

**Event:** June 2–3, 2026 | Fort Mason Center, San Francisco (~2,500 in-person + streaming)
**Theme:** "Be Yourself at Work" — AI agents adapt to how people work, not the reverse
**Narrative arc:** App era → Agent era. Six-layer agent stack: compute, models, context, tools, runtime, security.
**Book of News:** Replaced by [Microsoft Build Live blog](https://news.microsoft.com/build-2026-live-blog/microsoft-build-2026-live/)

## Key Facts

- **AI Builder credits are being SUNSET** — migrate existing deployments to Copilot Studio/Foundry now
- **Copilot Credits activation is OFF by default** — requires deliberate EA/admin opt-in
- **MAI routing in M365 Copilot is automatic** — Microsoft silently swaps OpenAI models for MAI where benchmarks match
- **Agent Builder** = lightweight no-code tier within M365 Copilot (not a separate product, not Copilot Studio)
- **AutoGen is in maintenance mode** — MAF 1.0 is the replacement path

## M365 Copilot

- Wave 3 rolling out (agentic capabilities in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Copilot Chat)
- **Cowork** — long-running multi-step work, uses Anthropic Claude (third-party model, notable)
- **ME7 (M365 E7)** GA May 1 — bundles E5 + M365 Copilot + Entra Suite + Agent 365, $99/user/month
- **Microsoft Scout** — always-on personal work agent (Frontier private preview) — Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint. Each agent runs under its own Entra identity.
- **Microsoft IQ** — unified context layer, GA June 2:
  - Work IQ (M365 signals), Fabric IQ (structured business data), Foundry IQ (unified retrieval), Web IQ (AI-native web grounding — new at Build)
- **Copilot Memory** — user preferences in public preview; /chronicle feature for standup summaries
- New M365 Copilot UI — task-aware workspace, not just a prompt box

## Copilot Studio

- **Computer-Using Agents (CUA)** — GA May 7, 2026. UI automation without APIs. Enterprise credential management. Adaptive interface recovery.
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)** — GA May 2026. Visual designer, no SDK required.
- **Real-time voice agents** — GA (North America/Dynamics 365 Contact Center)
- **MCP support** — PP July 2026 → GA July 2026. Auto-imports MCP tools as actions with existing enterprise security.
- **New Workflows experience** — Early Release/Preview. Visual canvas replacing linear flow designer. Intent-driven modular model.
- **New orchestration layer** — Early Release. 20% performance improvement, 50% token reduction.
- **Declarative agent manifest v1.7** — new editorial_answers, default_response_mode properties
- **Agent 365** — GA April 2026. Centralised control plane for multi-environment agent management.
- PVA is fully gone — it's all Copilot Studio now.

## Agent Builder (Clarified)

Not a new product. It is the lightweight, conversational, in-M365-Copilot creation surface for declarative agents only.
- Included in M365 Copilot licence (no Copilot Studio licence or credits required)
- No Actions, no external service integration — purely declarative
- Cannot be used in Teams Chat (current limitation)
- Microsoft says: "If you need Actions to integrate external services, use Copilot Studio"
- No major new announcements at Build 2026 — existing GA capability

## MAI Model Family (7 models, announced at Build)

| Model | Details | Status |
|-------|---------|--------|
| MAI-Thinking-1 | 35B reasoning, 256K context, claimed better than Claude Sonnet 4.6 | Private preview |
| MAI-Code-1 | Replaces GPT-4 in GitHub Copilot | GA |
| MAI-Code-1-Flash | 5B efficient, code completion | GA |
| MAI-Image-2.5 | Multimodal | Announced |
| MAI-Voice-2 | Voice | Announced |
| MAI-Transcribe-1.5 | Transcription | Announced |

All 7 will be open-sourced under permissive licenses.
Microsoft goal: self-sufficiency, 10x cost efficiency vs GPT-5.5 for specific workloads.

## Power Platform AI

- Power Automate: self-healing desktop flows (GA), Copilot Studio-powered actions in cloud flows (GA)
- Fabric Apps: coding agents build custom web apps from semantic model spec
- AI Builder: credits being sunset — functionality moving to Copilot Studio and Foundry
- MCP server for Power Automate process intelligence

## Azure AI Foundry (was Azure AI Studio)

- **Foundry IQ** — GA. Unified retrieval: Work IQ + Fabric IQ + File Search + Azure SQL + MCP
- **Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) 1.0** — GA April 2. Convergence of AutoGen + Semantic Kernel.
- **Hosted Agents** — GA July 2026. Per-session VM sandboxing, scale-to-zero, framework-agnostic.
- **Toolboxes** — Preview. Unified tool management (web, file, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A).
- **Tracing and Evaluations** — GA. OpenTelemetry-based, any framework.
- **Model catalogue** — 11,000+ models incl. GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8/Sonnet 4.5/Haiku 4.5, MAI, Fireworks
- **Fireworks AI on Foundry** — GA. Open-model inference under Azure enterprise SLAs.
- **Agent Optimizer** — Private preview. Production signals → ranked improvement candidates.

## Safety / Responsible AI

- Dedicated RA track at Build (structural signal)
- ASSERT (open source, GA) — policy-driven evaluation framework
- Agent Control Specification (open standard, GA) — portable governance framework
- Built-in content safety guardrails with Hosted Agents (GA July)
- Multi-turn Evaluation (preview) — catches safety regression across long conversations
- Runtime DLP for agent prompts (Preview)
- MDASH (Expanded Preview) — 100+ AI scanning agents, 96.55% CyberGym benchmark

## Windows / On-Device

- Copilot+ PC brand de-emphasised — pivot to universal local AI platform on any Windows hardware
- Recall API (new) — app access to local semantic index without raw screenshots; on-device, Hello-encrypted
- Windows Copilot Runtime expanding to all Windows 11 with compatible NPUs
- Windows Development Configurations GA
- RTX Spark Dev Box announced (NVIDIA compact AI dev workstation)

## Competitive Signals

- MAI-Thinking-1 claimed preferred over Claude Sonnet 4.6 (blind eval by Surge); matches Opus 4.6 on coding
- Mustafa Suleyman: "less concerned about Google, Meta, OpenAI" — Anthropic is the primary benchmark competitor
- Foundry positioned as model-neutral control plane (includes Anthropic + OpenAI models alongside MAI)
- "Project Polaris" — internal initiative to route MAI over OpenAI where performance is equivalent

## EA Governance Gaps (From ApertureOscillation)

1. **MAI model-swap is automatic** — M365 Copilot and Dynamics 365 will swap OpenAI for MAI silently where benchmarks match. Enterprise contracts assuming specific model versions need review.
2. **Copilot Credits off by default** — EA must own the activation decision; don't let individual teams enable it without governance.
3. **Shadow agent proliferation** — 3-tier authoring surface (Agent Builder / Copilot Studio / MAF) will produce ungoverned agents. Agent 365 registry + Intune policies are the control gate.
4. **AI Builder migration needed now** — credits being sunset, migrate to Copilot Studio/Foundry.
5. **AutoGen → MAF migration** — if any team is actively building on AutoGen, plan the migration path.

# Microsoft Build 2026 — Copilot Ecosystem Briefing

**Event:** June 2–3, 2026 | Fort Mason Center, San Francisco (~2,500 in-person + streaming)
**Theme:** "Be Yourself at Work" — agents adapt to how people work, not the reverse
**Strategic narrative:** App era → Agent era. Six-layer stack: compute · models · context · tools · runtime · security

---

## The Big Picture

Satya Nadella's message: *"Platforms don't shift on their own; developers build them forward."* Three major structural moves underpin everything:

1. **Microsoft is vertically integrating AI** — the MAI model family (7 in-house models announced) signals deliberate reduction of OpenAI dependency. Model routing is now automatic inside M365 Copilot and Dynamics 365.
2. **The agent authoring hierarchy is settled** — Agent Builder (no-code, in M365) → Copilot Studio (low-code) → Microsoft Agent Framework + Foundry (pro-code). These are three distinct tiers, not competitors.
3. **MCP is infrastructure now** — wired across Copilot Studio, Foundry, Teams, Windows, and Visual Studio simultaneously. It's the integration plumbing standard going forward.

---

## Microsoft 365 Copilot

**Wave 3** is rolling out through this period — agentic capabilities embedded in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Copilot Chat. No Wave 4 announced at Build; Wave 3 completion is the focus.

**New at Build:**

**Microsoft Scout** *(Frontier private preview)* — Microsoft's "always-on" personal work agent. Connects to Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint, calendar, contacts. Does meeting prep, scheduling conflict resolution, deliverable tracking, risk flagging (stalled decisions). Each Scout instance runs under its own Entra identity with Purview DLP enforced in real time. Requires Frontier enrollment + Intune policy + GitHub Copilot licence. Built on OpenClaw (open-source) + Work IQ.

**Microsoft IQ** *(GA as of June 2)* — Unified intelligence middleware sitting between enterprise data and all agents/Copilots:

| Layer | Status | What it does |
|-------|--------|---|
| Work IQ | GA | Semantic understanding of M365 signals within M365 trust boundary |
| Fabric IQ | GA, expanding | Structured business data from Fabric; now a first-party MCP tool |
| Foundry IQ | GA | Unified retrieval: Work IQ + Fabric IQ + File Search + Azure SQL + MCP |
| Web IQ | **New at Build** | AI-native web grounding — discovery, ranking, extraction; MCP-native |

**Agent 365 SDK** *(GA at Build)* — Framework-agnostic packages for Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, Azure AI Foundry. Free.

**M365 E7 (ME7)** *(GA May 1)* — Bundles E5 + M365 Copilot + Entra Suite + Agent 365 at $99/user/month.

**Copilot Memory** *(public preview)* — User-level preferences: communication style, tool stack, git conventions, etc. Admin governance controls included. `/chronicle` feature turns session history into standup summaries.

**Redesigned M365 Copilot UI** *(GA)* — Static prompt box replaced with a task-aware workspace. SharePoint connector now surfaces dynamic filters from Outlook, Teams, Azure DevOps, Google Drive, Jira, Confluence in real time.

**Cowork** *(rolling out)* — Long-running, multi-step work inside M365 productivity apps. Notable: Microsoft explicitly named **Anthropic Claude** as the model powering Cowork — significant admission of third-party model integration at the product level.

**Copilot Super App** — Teased but not shipped at Build. Nadella: *"Come summer... Chat, Cowork, and Code all in Copilot."* Watch for a summer announcement.

---

## Copilot Studio

The low-code/pro-code platform for building agents. Power Virtual Agents is fully gone — all roadmap content is under Copilot Studio.

### What GA'd at/around Build

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| **Computer-Using Agents (CUA)** | **GA May 7** | UI automation without APIs. Enterprise credential management — no embedded credentials. Adaptive interface recovery when UIs change. |
| **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)** | **GA May 2026** | Visual designer, no SDK required. Hub-and-spoke, peer-to-peer, hierarchical patterns supported. |
| **Real-time voice agents** | **GA** (North America, D365 Contact Center) | NLU, multilingual, consent-based recording. Pre-built templates for billing, orders, reservations. |
| **Analytics Viewer Role** | **GA Apr 28** | Read-only analytics access without configure rights. |
| **Agent 365 governance control plane** | **GA April** | Multi-environment management, PowerShell/Graph API, ITSM integration. |
| **CUA in multi-step workflows** | **Preview** | Combines UI automation, API calls, human approvals, business logic in one flow. |

### In Preview / Coming

| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| **MCP support in declarative agents** | PP July 2026 → GA July 2026 |
| New Workflows visual canvas | Early Release (Preview) |
| New orchestration layer (20% perf, 50% token reduction) | Early Release |
| Agent Nodes in Workflows (agent as workflow step) | PP April → GA September 2026 |
| M365 Copilot agent evaluation in Studio | PP July 2026 |
| Unified errors/warnings/governance view | PP May 15 → GA June 2026 |
| SharePoint lists as knowledge source | PP July → GA September 2026 |
| Copilot Credits activation | **OFF by default** — deliberate admin opt-in required |

### Extensibility Updates

- **MCP is now the primary integration pathway** alongside Power Platform connectors. MCP servers route through existing connector infrastructure — all existing DLP and auth controls apply automatically. Tools added/removed from MCP servers auto-sync to Copilot Studio.
- **Apps in Agents** *(GA, April)* — Rich interactive app experiences in Copilot Chat. Current partners: Adobe Express, Box, Figma, Monday.com, Wix.
- **Declarative agent manifest v1.7** — New `editorial_answers`, `default_response_mode`, `depends_on` properties. 8 new templates for common workplace scenarios.
- **GPT-5.5 in Copilot Studio** — Early Release (already available in Frontier).

### Governance (New in 2026)

- Block maker-provided credentials: PP now → GA August 2026
- Credential oversharing detection: PP July → GA September 2026
- **Agent Control Specification** — open standard for portable runtime governance, announced at Build
- Additional threat protection for agents: GA target June 2026

---

## Agent Builder — What It Actually Is

**Not a new product. Not Copilot Studio.** Agent Builder is the lightweight, conversational, no-code agent creation surface embedded directly inside Microsoft 365 Copilot (accessible from microsoft365.com/chat, office.com/chat, Teams desktop/web).

**What it does:** Describe what you want in natural language → it builds the declarative agent manifest. That's it.

**What it doesn't do:** Actions, external service integration, multi-agent orchestration, custom models.

**Licence:** Included in M365 Copilot — no additional Copilot Studio licence or Copilot Credits needed.

**Known limitation:** Agents created via Agent Builder cannot be used in Teams Chat.

**The hierarchy:**
```
Agent Builder          → no-code, in M365, declarative only, free with M365 Copilot
  ↓ need more?
Copilot Studio         → low-code, Actions, connectors, voice, orchestration, governance
  ↓ need custom model / complex orchestration?
MAF + Foundry          → pro-code, bring-your-own model, full agentic runtime
```

No major new Agent Builder announcements at Build 2026 — it's an existing GA capability.

| Copilot Studio-powered actions in cloud flows | **GA** |

| Fabric Apps (coding agents build web apps from semantic models) | **Announced at Build** |

Foundry is now the unified Azure AI control plane. Azure AI Studio branding is gone.

**GA at Build:**
- **Foundry IQ** — single SLA-backed retrieval endpoint. No custom RAG pipelines needed.
- **Foundry Toolkit for VS Code** — create, debug, deploy agents in one place
- **Voice Live** — real-time voice pipeline (STT, TTS, avatars, turn detection)
- **Fireworks AI on Foundry** — open-model inference under Azure enterprise SLAs, SOC 2, day-zero access to new open models
- **Tracing and Evaluations** — OpenTelemetry-based, any framework (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK, MAF)
- **Purview Data Risk Signals in Foundry** — real-time data security posture during agent testing

**GA July 2026:**
- **Hosted Agents** — managed runtime, per-session VM sandboxing, persistent filesystem, scale-to-zero, framework-agnostic

**Preview:**
- Toolboxes (unified tool management: web, file, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A), Memory (procedural/user/session), Routines, Tool search, MAI-Thinking-1, Rubric Evaluator, User Simulation, Multi-turn Evaluation

- **Agent ROI** *(private preview)* — task completion rates, time saved, cost efficiency translation

**Model catalogue:** 11,000+ models including GPT-5.5, GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5, full MAI family, Fireworks open models.

7 new models announced at Build. This is Microsoft's strategic bet on self-sufficiency.

| Model | Parameters | Benchmark claim | Status |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|--------|

| MAI-Image-2.5 | — | — | Announced |
| MAI-Voice-2 | — | — | Announced |
| MAI-Transcribe-1.5 | — | — | Announced |

All 7 will be open-sourced under permissive licences.

**"Project Polaris"** — internal initiative to route MAI models in place of OpenAI models where performance is equivalent or better. Projected 10x cost efficiency vs GPT-5.5 for specific workloads. **This routing is automatic** — not a customer choice — in M365 Copilot and Dynamics 365.

- **MAI-Code-1 / MAI-Code-1-Flash** replace GPT-4 for core autocomplete (GA)
- **GitHub Copilot native desktop app** — technical preview, Windows/Mac/Linux (requires subscription)
- **GitHub Copilot SDK** — GA in Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, Java
- Multi-agent workflows in VS Code shipped
- Microsoft IQ available across GitHub Copilot for enterprise grounding

The Copilot+ PC brand was conspicuously absent from the keynote — Microsoft pivoted to **"universal local AI platform on any Windows hardware"**.

🗒️ TASK: Explain MAI routing impact on Copilot Studio deployments

The honest answer: **it depends on which type of agent you've built.**

**Declarative agents (the most common Copilot Studio output)** are the ones most exposed. They run *on top of* M365 Copilot's orchestration engine — they don't bring their own model, they inherit the platform's. When Microsoft routes MAI in place of GPT models inside that engine, your declarative agents go along for the ride with no notification and no opt-out. The manifest defines topics, knowledge, actions — not the model. That's Microsoft's call.

**Custom engine agents** are insulated. You specified the model explicitly (via Foundry or Azure OpenAI Service). That endpoint is yours — Microsoft's internal routing decisions don't touch it. This is the main reason to consider custom engine for anything where model version matters: compliance evidence, reproducibility, regulated outputs.

**The practical exposure for a typical Copilot Studio estate:**

- Agents you built declaratively and published to Teams or M365 Copilot Chat → model can change under you
- Agents using CUA or A2A that still rely on platform orchestration → same exposure
- Anything grounding into Work IQ or Foundry IQ → those retrieval layers are Microsoft-controlled too, though the grounding quality is the concern there, not model identity

**What to actually do about it:**

1. Check whether any of your Copilot Studio agents have compliance or audit requirements tied to specific model behaviour (output format, response style, specific capabilities). If yes, those need to move to custom engine with an explicit Foundry endpoint.
2. For the rest — probably not a crisis. MAI-Thinking-1 benchmarks well and Microsoft's incentive is to make the swap invisible. The risk is a behaviour shift in edge cases, not a catastrophic failure.
3. If you need to evidence *what model processed a given interaction* for compliance, declarative agents on M365 Copilot cannot give you that today regardless of MAI. That's a governance gap that predates Build 2026.

The short version: declarative agents inherit platform model routing by design — that's a feature, not a bug, until you have a reason it matters. Custom engine agents are your lever if it does matter.

🗣️ JellyPai: Declarative agents inherit platform routing silently; custom engine agents are the isolation lever if compliance requires model pinning.
